title: Free Night Awards Training Q&A: The Stay-Nights Reduction on Late-Cancellation Losses
content:
These questions explain the stay-nights reduction of the stay's protected value, which applies to one of the Free Night Awards forfeited on a reservation cancelled after its deadline.

**What is the rule?**
The stay-nights reduction of the stay's protected value is the upper stay-nights reduction, 2000 points, when the stay night credits posted to the member's Ashbury Rewards account in the last twelve months add up to at least the upper stay-credit nights, 40 nights; the lower stay-nights reduction, 1000 points, when they add up to at least the lower stay-credit nights, 20 nights; and nothing otherwise. The reduction is taken off the stay's protected value once.

| Stay night credits of the last twelve months | Stay-nights reduction |
|---|---|
| 40 nights or more | 2000 points |
| 20 to 39 nights | 1000 points |
| 19 nights or fewer | None |

**Which credits count?**
The night credits posted to the Ashbury Rewards account for stays, that is, night credit postings whose source is stay nights, summed by their nights. Card anniversary night credits are not stay night credits and do not count.

**What are the last twelve months?**
The credits posted fewer than twelve whole calendar months before the loss, counted from each credit's posting date to the date of the loss.

**How does the window treat a credit posted on the same day number a year earlier?**
For a hypothetical loss dated 6 October, a stay night credit posted on 7 October of the previous year is eleven whole calendar months old and counts; one posted on 6 October of the previous year is twelve whole calendar months old and does not count.

**A worked example (hypothetical account)?**
In the window the account shows stay night credits of 12, 9 and 4 nights and a card anniversary night credit of 15 nights. The stay night credits add up to 25 nights, at least 20 and fewer than 40, so the stay-nights reduction is 1000 points; the card anniversary credit is not added.
